newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian think tank proposes bad bank layoff plan.
newsitem.headline: Italian think tank proposes bad bank layoff plan.

text.p: The cost of cutting back Italy's bloated banking industry could be tackled by each bank creating its own ad hoc company to deal with slimming down the work force, Italian economic research institute Prometeia said.

Antonio Rigon, a banking specialist with Prometeia, told a conference that until now Italian banks had toyed with ideas which involved sharing the cost of downsizing the sector among all banks, even relatively healthy ones.
Italy's banking association has said that the industry needs to lay off at least 30,000 employees in the coming years if it is to stay competitive.

Rigon said that each bank should set up its own "bad bank" to pay for staff layoffs. The advantage would be that restructuring costs would not be consolidated with the bank's profit and loss account and would therefore not have a negative impact on return on equity.
Employees nearing the end of their careers would be transferred to the bad bank from the parent which would ensure that enough business was placed with the offshoot to pay for salaries, said Rigon.
